page.text:
The entirety of classical mathematics can be systematically constructed
from a single primitive notion—the *set*—and a single primitive binary
relation—*membership*, denoted by $\in$. Numbers, algebraic structures,
geometric spaces, and continuous functions are not independent
ontological primitives; rather, each is formally realized as a set
equipped with relations that are themselves collections of ordered pairs.
This chapter establishes the axiomatic foundation of this universe, known
as Zermelo--Fraenkel set theory (ZF), and introduces the fundamental
operations that govern set formation.
